Subject: Post-demo: token capacity, latency impact & fallbacks (Axiom Analytics)

Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying items so our SRE/SE teams can scope a canary: 

TL;DR: we heard you want p95 response time <= 300ms for the inference endpoint under typical user flows, sustained during peak analytics runs with up to ~120 concurrent inference sessions. You also indicated some responses can be streamed (progressive transcripts) but many will be full-document summaries where output length may hit 1.5–2k tokens.

Key questions we need from you to finalize the technical plan: 
- Typical input size distribution (tokens) for your customer documents: 75% < 2k tokens, 20% between 2k–6k, 5% > 6k? Please confirm or provide a small sample.
- Desired max output tokens per request and what percent of requests require streaming vs single final response.
- Is occasional p99 spike tolerance acceptable (if so, how long) or do we need strict p99 SLA?

Immediate next steps we propose: 
1) Laura will produce a short performance matrix estimating p50/p95 latency across three context window bands and two model variants (baseline and quantized).
2) We’ll draft a canary plan with routing/fallback rules: prefer streaming where output > 512 tokens, otherwise allow batched micro-batches to hit latency SLOs.
3) Marissa will set up procurement/billing triggers for a short Dedicated slot for the PoC if you want predictable throughput.

I attached the one-pager we referenced and a blank perf matrix for you to fill if you prefer. If anything above is off, flag it and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — Karthik

Tom/Karthik — following up with the detailed technical readout we discussed. I ran back-of-envelope numbers from our runtime on a T4/80GB-equivalent Dedicated slot (representative of the PoC hardware we suggested). Notes below are conservative and assume no prefix cache for the long inputs; if you can reuse cache or prefix stitching, numbers improve materially.

Performance matrix (high level):
- Model A (high-accuracy, larger): single-token gen cost ~0.7ms/token; Model B (smaller quantized): ~0.25ms/token.
- Network + orchestration overhead: ~40–60ms p50 baseline for short requests (sub-256 tokens output).

Representative scenarios (end-to-end p95 approximate):
1) Short input (<=512 tokens), short output (<=128 tokens) — Model B: p95 ~120ms, Model A: p95 ~220ms.
2) Medium input (2k tokens), output (512 tokens) — Model B: p95 ~360ms, Model A: p95 ~820ms.
3) Large context (6k tokens), output (1.5k tokens) — streaming enabled: first chunks p95 ~420ms, full finalization p95 ~2.1s on Model A; Model B finalization ~850–1.2s depending on batching and KV cache effectiveness.

Observations and tradeoffs:
- Context window grows KV cache and attention work roughly quadratically in naive attention; our runtime mitigates this with block-sparse kernels but latency still increases nonlinearly beyond ~4k tokens.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for users (first tokens appear quickly) but does not change total compute needed to produce long outputs. For your p95 SLA of <=300ms, streaming helps for early UX but cannot make a 1.5k-token finalization complete within 300ms unless you use a smaller model or aggressive truncation.
- Concurrency impact: with 120 concurrent sessions, sustained, we need either Dedicated capacity with multi-GPU autoscaling or to throttle concurrency per customer (we recommend 50–80 concurrent per reserved pool and overflow to burst capacity).

Suggested fallback strategy (canary rules):
- If expected output > 512 tokens and user experience tolerates progressive results -> enable streaming and set a soft p95 guidance for first-chunk <= 300ms.
- If strict final p95 <= 300ms required -> enforce output cap at 512 tokens or route to Model B (quantized) with cost/quality tradeoff and notify client of reduced fidelity.
- If queue depth > 30 requests waiting -> trigger routing to lower-cost model variants and/or return a limited summary with a follow-up async job for full draft (webhook to Axiom when ready).

I attached a perf matrix (xlsx) with these scenarios filled; you can paste your empirical input distribution and I’ll return updated latency projections.

Action items: 
- Tom: share 200 anonymized example documents (s3 link or sample zip) so we can run a small benchmark.
- Karthik: confirm whether Axiom needs guaranteed p99 SLA for the PoC.
- Marissa: prepare a tentative Dedicated sizing (2×80GB GPUs with autoscale) and costs for a 4-week PoC.

Happy to jump on 30–45 minute technical call with your infra team to walk through kernel/attention implications.

Thanks — Laura

Thanks — this is super helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We can provide the sample set; will export 250 docs (mix of short/medium/long). Expect most to be 1–3k tokens.
- Our product requirement: interactive analysts should see first results within 300ms (first chunk). Final full summaries can be async if they exceed 800ms, but customers will pay a premium if the final is <500ms.
- p99 is not required for PoC; p95 is the main gating metric for user-facing paths.

Can you outline a minimal canary plan that hits these constraints (first-chunk <=300ms for >80% of requests, ability to process 100 concurrent analysts at peak) and what model routing rules we should adopt during the PoC? Also please include cost ballpark for 2-week Dedicated slot.

Tom

Tom — looping in procurement/ops items and proposing concrete next steps. Attached: axiom_perf_matrix.xlsx (filled with Laura's numbers) and the Redwood streaming playbook (short checklist).

Minimal canary plan (2-week):
- Provision: 2×80GB GPUs reserved (Dedicated) with autoscale policy to +1 GPU at 70% utilization.
- Routing rules: 
  * Default: Model B (quantized) with streaming enabled for outputs > 256 tokens. First-chunk goal <=300ms.
  * Escalation: If client marks response quality below threshold in QA set, route those sessions to Model A for reprocessing and log differences.
- Concurrency: soft limit 100 concurrent analyst sessions per pool; overflow routed to burst pool with higher latency alerts.
- Fallbacks: enforce output cap at 1.5k tokens for interactive path; larger exports kick off an async job with webhook notification.
- Observability: dashboard with token-distribution heatmap, p50/p95/p99 per route, and a per-request token trace for root-cause.

Estimated cost (2 weeks, Dedicated baseline): ~$18k–$26k depending on actual sustained utilization and storage for KV cache; I’ll put a firm quote after we get expected concurrency and token distribution.

Next actions: 
- Tom: drop S3 link for sample set (target by 8/13).
- Karthik: I’ll draft PO and a short Statement of Work for the PoC.
- Laura: schedule 30-minute infra deep-dive with Axiom on 8/14 or 8/16.

If that aligns, we’ll spin up the Dedicated pool and run a 48-hour microbenchmark on your samples before the formal PoC window.

Cheers — Marissa
